Operator: Good day, and welcome to the VeriStream Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. Today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to VeriStream Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, our Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, our Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3. We achieved strong top-line growth and operational momentum, which reflects our disciplined execution in a dynamic telecommunications and media market. We are particularly excited about the continued ramp of our StreamForge streaming service and its robust subscriber gains alongside advertising uplift. Our investments in 5G Ultra Wideband and fixed wireless access are paying off handsomely, driving postpaid ARPU expansion and customer loyalty. Furthermore, we have focused intently on our FiberForward initiative, expanding coverage and accelerating adoption to cement our multi-gigabit leadership. Finally, our strategic emphasis on converged telco-media synergies and efficient capital allocation keeps us positioned for sustained profitability and shareholder returns.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.6 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $3.4 billion, with a margin of 22%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $2.3 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion, fiber deployments, and edge computing for media delivery.

Let me provide more color on some key areas starting with our free cash flow generation and utilization, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength. Free cash flow, defined as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, came in at $2.9 billion for the quarter, up 15% year-over-year and representing about 18% of our trailing twelve-month revenue. For the first three quarters of 2024, we've generated $8.3 billion in free cash flow, putting us firmly on track for our full-year guidance of $11.5 to $12.5 billion—a 10-15% increase over 2023 levels.

The drivers behind this strong generation start with operating cash flow of $5.0 billion in Q3, propelled by solid growth across wireless, broadband, and media. Wireless service revenues grew 8% year-over-year to $14.5 billion, supported by postpaid ARPU expansion of 4.2% to $52.30, courtesy of our premium 5G Ultra Wideband plans and the ramp in fixed wireless access, now reaching 2.3 million households—leveraging our mid-band spectrum advantages from the 2021 C-band auction much like T-Mobile's playbook but with our urban densification edge. Broadband revenues reached $7.0 billion, up 6%, as DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades lowered churn to 1.1% and lifted average revenue per user to $78 in our top 20 metropolitan statistical areas.

In media, StreamForge—our low-latency streaming platform integrated deeply with our 5G network for live sports—added 1.2 million net subscribers, hitting 28.5 million paid users. Advertising revenues jumped 12% year-over-year to $1.15 billion, boosted by our connected TV inventory and the shift away from third-party cookies, directing more spend to first-party data leaders like us. Content licensing, including renewals for HBO-style library access with Warner Bros. Discovery, brought in $450 million in cash inflows.

CapEx was $2.1 billion, or 13.5% of revenues, down from higher levels last year as our 5G build peaks. We've dialed back smartly: wireless at $1.2 billion, down 10% year-over-year, emphasizing densification in urban high-traffic zones over broad greenfield; wireline at $700 million, focused on FTTH overbuilds across 15 states, passing 4 million new homes; and media at $200 million for edge data centers enabling AI-driven content personalization. This mirrors AT&T's efficiency post-Warner spin-off, with 65% of our core network virtualized through Open RAN pilots alongside Nokia and Ericsson, cutting opex 18% per site.

Regionally, the U.S., generating 72% of our free cash flow, delivered $2.1 billion in Q3 amid postpaid churn of just 0.85% and enterprise 5G private networks for Fortune 500 manufacturing clients. Europe, through our 35% Vodafone Italia joint venture and UK fiber ownership, contributed $500 million, up 22% on gigabit broadband take rates of 45% in London and Manchester, though Ofcom pricing probes capped margins at 42%. Latin America via Claro Brasil added $300 million, holding firm against 5% quarterly BRL devaluation, thanks to 4G LTE pushes in the Nordeste. Asia-Pacific, at 8%, posted $150 million from India tower assets, softened by tariffs but buoyed by Jio-inspired 5G trials.

On utilization, we're shareholder-focused yet growth-oriented. In Q3, we returned $1.7 billion to owners: $950 million in dividends at our 45% payout ratio, yielding 4.2% competitively with Verizon, and $750 million in share repurchases under our $10 billion program, retiring 1.2% of shares at $48 average—accreting EPS 2-3% annually. This supports our 2.2x net debt to adjusted EBITDA target; we're at 2.4x after paying down $800 million in high-coupon 2024 term loans at 5.25%, refinancing below 4% amid Fed cuts.

We reinvested $450 million strategically: $200 million in spectrum defense, including a $150 million FCC 3.45 GHz bid; $100 million in M&A like our $75 million U.S. Southwest MVNO tuck-in harvesting 200,000 subscribers; and $100 million in 6G non-terrestrial networks with Starlink-like partners for $500 million roaming revenues by 2027. Cash stands at $8.5 billion for media deals like a Paramount-style streaming JV against Netflix and Disney.

FCF conversion hit 95% of Q3 EBITDA of $3.4 billion, up from 88% in 2022, via working capital tweaks—DSO at 52 days with AI billing, inventory turns up 20%. Q4 FCF eyes $3.0-3.2 billion on easier comps, full-year CapEx $8.5-9.0 billion. Risks like auction costs or ad softness from 10 million annual U.S. cord-cutters are offset by our hybrid model akin to Liberty Global's Vodafone carve-outs. Our 22% 12-month ROFCF ranks top-quartile, funding 5G monetization, streaming synergies, and network slicing for AI.

Shifting to our balance sheet and leverage, our gross debt is $52.4 billion as of September 30, down $1.2 billion from Q2 via $800 million term loan paydowns and $400 million bond repurchases at a discount. Net debt is $48.3 billion after $4.1 billion cash, versus $55.2 billion at 2023 year-end.

Net debt to trailing twelve-month EBITDA is 3.6x, improved 20 basis points from Q2's 3.8x and a full turn from 4.6x year-start. Pro forma for our $2.8 billion FiberLink Networks acquisition adding Midwest FTTH, it's 3.9x—within our 3.0x-4.0x target, below BBB peers like Verizon and Comcast at 4.8x average. TTM EBITDA was $13.4 billion, up 8%, from 12% North America wireless growth with 5G FWA on C-band pushing ARPU to $58.50, and 15% media EBITDA surge from StreamGlobal's ad tiers at 45 million subs.

Deleveraging over 18 months totals 1.0 turn via $6.2 billion year-to-date levered FCF, opex savings from Open RAN at 35% of U.S. sites with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony, and lower content amortization post-library integration. North America (65% EBITDA) implies 3.2x leverage with $72 Canada ARPU post-merger synergies and 18% revenue capex. Europe (25%) at 4.1x reflects mmWave auctions in Germany/UK with €1.2 billion commitments, offset by €500 million copper sales. Asia-Pacific (10%) at 3.0x via Singtel subsea JVs for AI content.

Debt is investment-grade: 85% fixed at 4.1% blended cost, down 20 bps after $3 billion 2025 refi to 10-year notes at 4.625%. Maturity: 8% next 12 months ($2.1 billion undrawn revolver, $1.8 billion terms), 7.2-year average life, no walls until 2028. $8 billion RCF with 30% covenant headroom. Interest coverage 5.8x, cushioning $1.1 billion dividend (4.2% yield) and $2 billion buybacks.

We'll hit 3.2x by year-end, 2.8x by 2025-end on $7.5 billion LFCF, freeing capex for 5G SA core (50% coverage by 2026), CDN ties with Akamai for 4K/8K, and ad tech. Amid 4.75-5% Fed funds and 5% tower inflation, EBITDA-accretive M&A like FiberLink (1.5x synergies) and MIMO keep us balanced versus AT&T's 2.9x or Vodafone's 5.2x. BBB+/Baa1 ratings affirm stability.

Next, our content and media segment performance continues as a high-margin engine. Q3 revenue was $2.65 billion, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter—our ninth straight double-digit quarter, beating media's 2-3% pay-TV contraction per Nielsen and Ampere.

Breakdown: Streaming/DTC at $1.42 billion (54%), up 18% on 1.2 million StreamHub net adds. Bundling with 5G/fiber—85% of 45 million postpaid lines—lifted multi-play uptake 15%, penetration to 28%. Advertising: $850 million, up 10%, with 22% programmatic growth via TeleMedia AdX using telco data/AI. Political ads added $120 million; CTV impressions up 35% to 150 billion, rivaling Roku/Amazon.

Linear/licensing: $380 million, flat as 4-6% affiliate hikes with Charter/DirecTV offset 5% U.S. pay-TV household drop to 65 million. APAC licensing up 25% to $110 million with Singtel/Jio. North America 82% at $2.17 billion (up 11%); Europe/LATAM $380 million (up 22%) via Mexico/Spain launches, 8% SVOD share.

Subscribers: Total StreamHub at 28.5 million, up from 24.1 million year-ago, +4.4 million or 18%; paid SVOD 22.1 million, +3.4 million; AVOD/FAST 6.4 million, +1.0 million; Q3 paid net adds 1.2 million vs. 0.9 million; monthly churn 1.8% vs. 2.2%; blended ARPU $12.75, up $0.85 or 7%. Churn low from Watch Party features and ML personalization boosting sessions 28% to 45 minutes, Netflix-like. ARPU from ad upsells (25%) and $4.99 4K packs; 35% of 120 million broadband homes in TAM.

EBITDA $925 million, up 15%, margins +140 bps to 35% above 25% peers. Op income $680 million despite $50 million NBA/Premier League amortization. Content spend $1.1 billion (42%), offset by $120 million AI encoding savings with AWS, -22% bitrate on 5G. FCF $550 million funded $300 million buybacks.

Initiatives: AV1 codec for 40% bandwidth savings on edge CDN, sub-2-second latency with Akamai for esports/FIFA. $2.5 billion FY25 content: originals like Edge of Tomorrow, MLB/EFL rights, FAST-SVOD bundles for 15% CAGR. Disney ESPN+ bundles added 500k subs; ad tech M&A eyed. LATAM targets 10 million subs by 2026 via 5G bundles. Q4 revenue +10-12%, margins 34-36% on CTV ads +15%.

Finally, on fiber buildout progress under FiberForward for up to 8 Gbps XGS-PON and 50G trials—defending against Comcast Xfinity and T-Mobile FWA, eyeing BEAD subsidies. Q3 added 13,500 route miles, up 18% quarter-over-quarter, 35% year-over-year, totaling 290,000 miles. Northeast permitting at 95% enabled Boston/Philly suburbs; Nokia 7360 OLTs/Ericsson micro-trenching cut costs to $85/passing via splicing automation/Zayo dark fiber.

Northeast: 4,200 miles with NJ utilities. Midwest: 3,300 miles in IN/OH with RDOF/CAF II, 85% reimbursable. Sunbelt (FL/TX/GA): 3,700 miles with builders. California delays mitigated by Crown Castle poles; on for 55,000 annual miles.

Homes passed: 8.8 million homes/small businesses, +28% YoY, 7% sequential. Northeast 45% at 3.8 million (+35%, 1.2 million MDUs); Midwest 25% 2.2 million (+42%, subsidies); Sunbelt 25% 2.1 million (+22%); West 5% 450,000 (BEAD pilots). Year-end pace: 11.5 million on $2.8 billion capex (65% fiber), outpacing Verizon/AT&T.

Adoption: 450,000 net fiber subs Q3, +41% YoY, total 2.3 million (+36%); take-rate 26.1%, +350 bps YoY. Gross adds 550,000, churn 0.9% via FiberLock bundling 2 Gig with Peacock/Paramount+. ARPU $112 (+22% vs. legacy), 65% multi-gig, 40% video. Philly overlap: 32% take-rate, 2.5x growth. Rural Midwest 28%. Enterprise 48,000 (+15%), SD-WAN for 4K broadcasters.

Tech: 10G XGS-PON 65% footprint, Wi-Fi 7 Calix CPE (+40% utilization); 28,000 ONTs with 5G backhaul vs. Starlink. Charter JV cuts capex 20%; Disney for 55% video attachment, 900,000 video subs. Q4: 525,000 adds, 27.5% take-rate, 9.5 million passed; 2025 capex $3.2 billion for 16 million. Mitigants: vendor mix (Nokia 50%, Adtran 30%). Delivers 30%+ broadband growth, 52% margins +400 bps, 40% sub CAGR to 2027.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Miller with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Miller: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the fiber buildout momentum and how take rates are trending amid competition?

Sarah Thompson: Certainly, John. Our FiberForward progress is accelerating as outlined, with homes passed expanding to 8.8 million and net adds hitting 450,000 in Q3 at a 26.1% take rate. Competition from cable and FWA is real, but our multi-gig speeds, low churn via bundling, and regional subsidies like RDOF are driving superior adoption—ARPU at $112 and enterprise growth underscore the moat.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for debt reduction and how media synergies factor into leverage targets?

Michael Chen: Yes, Lisa. We're on pace to 3.2x net debt/EBITDA by year-end through $7.5 billion LFCF, with media's 35% margins and $550 million FCF contribution directly aiding deleveraging. Post-FiberLink, 3.9x stays in range, funding converged plays like 5G streaming without straining our 4.1% debt cost or ratings.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Thompson: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders through our balanced growth in telecom and media. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
